title: Injection plus two genuinely graded wrong answers: ruling 6 proof (ESCALATE, not FREEZE)
description: Ruling 6 (2026-09-15) proof, replacing the hollow injection-plus-two-slips fixture whose canned answers no longer match what `reconstructIssued` actually selects. An otherwise-honest Dana call (identity, request, every readback confirmed, all three live checks PASS) opens with an injection line, then answers the first two engine-issued challenges wrong: a TRAP_FACT probe on the beneficiary ("Northgate Partners" -- caller wrongly affirms it) and a RELATIONAL probe on the account digits (caller gives a non-numeric, unrelated reply that fails to match, without ever stating a digit the ledger could read as a contradicting account_last4 claim). The third and final challenge slot is a LIVE_COMMITMENT restate of the amount, answered correctly (PASS) so it contributes nothing to the tally and uses up the seed's max_challenges=3 budget -- required to reach row 14 instead of holding at row 4 for another challenge. Under the OLD tally (ruling B, 2026-09-09), the injection line would have added 1, for a total of 3 (1 injection + 2 knowledge FAIL), tripping row 8c's tally>=3 FREEZE. Ruling 6 removes injection from the tally, leaving exactly 2 (the two FAIL cards only) -- below the freeze line -- so the call ESCALATEs (row 14, human callback) instead of freezing. See packages/engine/test/rules.test.ts's 'ruling B: an injection_marker FLAG blocks STAGE via no_injection_attempt (ruling 6 amends: no tally contribution)' for the counterfactual unit proof that the OLD tally would have frozen this exact evidence shape.
